known_limitations: This is a single-language (Java) shard; the frozen common-basis figure for Semantic Locality (spec: interaction_with_quality_metrics.common_basis_rule) requires the runner to intersect this probe-by-probe fragment existence with the other 9 languages' shards and recompute the metric restricted to the common basis. The all-fragments figure above (88.2, n_L=41) is the correct provisional Java figure and is explicitly labeled as such per the spec's dual-basis publication requirement.

Lookup counts reflect this worker's mechanical application of R10/R5 and standard JDK documentation; they were not produced by compiling and running each fragment under the frozen toolchain (packet-only mode, no local build tools available), so V1 (build/run verification) evidence for these Java fragments must still be produced by a build-capable worker before these entries can be treated as fully audited.

The cap-of-7 normalization denominator is this worker's documented, symmetric choice (matching the 7 lookup-kind categories named in methodology 6.1.3.C) since the methodology text does not itself freeze a specific normalization divisor for this metric; it must be applied identically to all languages by whichever worker computes their locality shards, and the runner should verify cross-shard consistency of this constant before aggregation.
evidence.measurement_note: This shard measures Java only, as assigned. Per capability_universe.json interaction_with_quality_metrics, metrics A-D are computed on a COMMON BASIS across all 10 languages, determined at aggregation time by the runner from all language shards. The figures below are the Java-side raw and per-probe data required for that aggregation; the runner must intersect this with the other 9 languages' NONE/support results before computing the final common-basis figure. A provisional Java-only aggregate (all-fragments basis, n_L=41 of 44) is reported here for audit and is NOT itself the final common-basis Semantic Locality score.
evidence.methodology_reference: semantic_compression.md section 6.1.3.C; capability_universe.json probes[] and support_rubric; semantic_site_matrix.json probes[].sites[]
evidence.normalization_rule: Semantic Compression methodology (6.1.3.C) mandates recording raw lookup counts and states 'lower lookup cost is better' but does not freeze a specific 0-100 normalization formula for this metric. This worker applies, and documents for auditability, a symmetric linear normalization pinned before language-specific annotation of this shard: per-probe lookup counts are capped at 7 (the number of distinct lookup kinds enumerated in the methodology: callee signature, variable declaration, type declaration, overload set, trait/interface implementation, imported definition, global configuration/compiler mode), score_probe = 100 * (1 - min(lookups,7)/7), and the language's aggregate = 100 * (1 - mean(lookups)/7) computed over the all-fragments basis (n_L). This same formula is intended to be applied identically to every language's shard so no language receives a different cap or scale.

per_probe.basis: local, immutable primitive binding; mutability/type/init all explicit in the two-line fragment
static field + static final constant, both annotated explicitly at declaration
Java definite-assignment analysis is fully local to the method body
P-a substitution: Java arrays are always zero-initialized (new byte[16]); the zero-fill is IMPLICIT (JLS default), not a lookup
x++ / x+=1 on a local; overflow wrap is IMPLICIT JLS behavior, not a declaration lookup
xs.set(1,42): 1 hop to xs's own declaration (given context) to confirm its declared mutable List type; 1 hop to List.set's documented in-place/exception behavior
Collections.unmodifiableList(xs): 1 hop to xs's declaration; 1 hop to Collections.unmodifiableList javadoc to confirm non-copying view + write-rejection
== on a user-defined reference type is fixed-by-JLS identity comparison; no operator overloading in Java, so no lookup needed
bare call f(x): per R5, f's declaration is 'given elsewhere' and excluded from tokens but counted as 1 non-local lookup to resolve aliasing/mutation outcome
lambda capturing k, applied via Stream.map or manual loop; 1 hop to the standard higher-order operation's documented behavior
xs.get(1): 1 hop to List.get javadoc to determine reference-vs-copy semantics of the returned boxed element
local record DivMod(int q,int r) declared in-fragment; record-pattern deconstruction (Java 21) destructures q,r in one local construct
a*b+c fully local; JLS precedence/width fixed
integer division truncates toward zero and % follows dividend sign by fixed JLS rule, no external lookup
Math.addExact(m,1) in try/catch (rung i): 1 hop to java.lang.Math.addExact documented overflow-throw behavior
local guard on b==0 (rung ii); no external lookup needed
s1.equals(s2): 1 hop to java.lang.String.equals javadoc confirming content, not identity, comparison
xs.sort(Comparator.reverseOrder()): 1 hop to Comparator.reverseOrder javadoc; 1 hop to List.sort javadoc confirming in-place mutation
explicit narrowing cast (int) big (rung ii, since Math.toIntExact throws rather than returning an optional/error value so rung i is unavailable); JLS-fixed truncation, no lookup
i + d triggers JLS binary numeric promotion of i to double; fixed rule, no lookup
xs.get(i) on ArrayList: 1 hop to ArrayList.get javadoc confirming IndexOutOfBoundsException on out-of-range index
xs.subList(1,4): 1 hop to xs's declaration; 1 hop to List.subList javadoc confirming it is a live view backed by the original list
Optional.empty()/orElse(0): 1 hop to java.util.Optional javadoc
o.map(...): 1 hop to Optional.map javadoc confirming short-circuit on empty
Integer.parseInt(s) propagating unchecked NumberFormatException: 1 hop to Integer.parseInt javadoc (unchecked exceptions carry no declaration-site signal in Java)
try/catch(NumberFormatException): 1 hop to Integer.parseInt javadoc to know the specific exception type to catch
sealed interface Shape permits Circle, Rect declared with its two record implementations in the same fragment; closedness is locally visible via the permits clause
pattern-matching switch over sealed Shape: 1 hop to Shape's own declaration (from F14.P1, outside this probe's fragment) to confirm the permits set the compiler is exhaustiveness-checking against
non-sealed Shape interface in a separate 'shapes' unit, Tri implementing it from a second unit: 1 hop to Shape's interface declaration/signature
generic method <T> T head(List<T> xs) declared in-fragment; both call sites and combination are local
<T extends Comparable<T>> max_of: 1 hop to java.lang.Comparable's compareTo contract
interface Named plus A,B and the heterogeneous List<Named> and dispatching call are all declared within the measured fragment
xs.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum(): 1 hop to Stream/IntStream.sum documented behavior
Map iteration + getOrDefault: 1 hop confirming iteration order is unspecified for the chosen Map implementation; 1 hop to Map.getOrDefault javadoc
try (var in = new FileReader(...)): 1 hop to confirm FileReader implements Closeable/AutoCloseable for try-with-resources

Handle implements AutoCloseable, closed via try-with-resources block exit: 1 hop to AutoCloseable/try-with-resources semantics; this is FULL (not a finalize()-based substitute) because 'close-on-scope-exit' is one of the canonical_task's own accepted deterministic hooks
System.out.println: java.lang is implicitly imported; no explicit import declaration and no external lookup needed to resolve availability
external qualified call util.Util.pubAdd(2,3) against a separate package/unit: 1 hop to the util.Util class declaration
CompletableFuture.supplyAsync + join: 1 hop to CompletableFuture API contract; 1 hop to join's blocking-wait semantics
AtomicLong.incrementAndGet from two threads + join: 1 hop to AtomicLong's documented atomicity guarantee; 1 hop to Thread.join semantics
java.lang.foreign (Panama FFM API) call to C abs(): 1 hop to Linker.nativeLinker contract; 1 hop to FunctionDescriptor/MethodHandle invocation semantics; 1 hop to SymbolLookup resolution semantics

evidence.raw_measure_definition: For each probe, raw locality lookups = count of required external semantic lookups/declaration-graph hops (callee signature, variable declaration, type declaration, overload set, trait/interface implementation, imported definition, global configuration/compiler mode) needed to resolve the probe's frozen semantic_site_matrix facts for Java, beyond what is available from the measured_fragment's local surface form. EXPLICIT_LOCAL and IMPLICIT-classified facts contribute 0 (IMPLICIT means the language spec fixes the behavior without requiring any declaration-graph hop; it is captured instead by Hidden Semantic Cost, not Locality). Probes scored NONE for Java (no fragment exists) are excluded from the average per the interaction_with_quality_metrics common-basis handling for that language's own figures, and are recorded separately.
